new_issues.title: `send(event, wait=True)` resolves with `changed=False, error=None` for an event held by `onUnhandled: "defer"`
`Event(system=True)` is user-settable and bypasses `strict`, `onUnhandled` and the `"*"` matcher on both engines
Event provenance does not survive a snapshot: restored engine events become user traffic and fail a machine configured `onUnhandled: "error"`
A pending `ErrorEvent` / `DoneEvent` is silently dropped by `get_persisted_snapshot()` — an accepted invoke failure vanishes with no record
The sync `maxIterations` `tripped` flag is scoped to the drain, not the chain — one runaway starves every later unrelated event in the same batch (#77)
The `sync=` compatibility shim treats a `**kwargs` clock as consent and feeds it an unexpected keyword (#76)
`max_iterations` does not bound an action-side `send()` on the async engine; the #77 parity claim covers the `raise` built-in only
The alias-ambiguity guard does not fire for its own documented example (`fetchData` required, `fetch_data` + `fetchData` registered)
`resolve_aliases` mutates the caller's `MachineLogic` registry, suppressing the ambiguity guard for later machines and retroactively rebinding earlier ones
The `logic_modules` normalised index uses `setdefault`, so duplicate snake/camel implementations resolve by module iteration order with no error
A `done.invoke` from a sync service is classed as self-generated; after a trip the completion is dropped and the machine parks in the invoking state (#77)
The library trips its own `ErrorEvent.data` `DeprecationWarning` from `plugins.py` and `base_interpreter.py`, breaking `-W error::DeprecationWarning` CI
`_resolve_event_spec` builds an `Event` whose `payload` is the exception object, not a dict — `event.payload.get(...)` raises `AttributeError`
`escalate` is the one failure path not converted to `ErrorEvent`; handlers written to the documented `event.error` pattern get `AttributeError`
Strict mode still exempts by name: `done.invoke.NEVER_INVOKED`, `after.party`, `xstate.whatever` and `___xstate_forged` all pass undeclared
`SyncInterpreter` never delivers `onError` for a failed invoked child machine; the parent parks in the invoking state
